clue.text: South African flower colour

definitions.meaning: a flower is something that flows, a river
the shade between red and yellow

explanation.definitionFit: The Orange River runs across South Africa, and the same name is the hue of a ripe tangerine.

clue.text: Love to donate a window

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
to donate is to give

explanation.surface: A lover offers to pay for a church window.
explanation.walkthrough: An ogive is a pointed Gothic arch, and by extension a window built in that shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogive is the pointed arch of Gothic architecture, used for lancet windows.

clue.text: Unopened hair spray

parts.note: hair lacquer still sealed in its pressurised can, the container that sprays it out

explanation.definitionFit: Hair lacquer is sold in a pressurised spray can of that name.

clue.text: On drugs maybe, the Spanish provide the weed

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of the two words beside it are only one possible arrangement

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine form of the

explanation.surface: Someone high on narcotics, with some Spaniards, hands out marijuana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is the anagram signal on 'On drugs'. 'Weed' beside 'drugs' suggests cannabis, but it is a garden plant.

clue.text: Mother rejected Lamb and read Fielding's work

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for mother is read backwards

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name Elia

explanation.surface: A mother turns down a lamb dinner and settles down with a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns MA into AM. Lamb is the essayist Charles Lamb, not the animal. Henry Fielding's last novel was Amelia (1751).
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding published the novel Amelia in 1751, his final full-length fiction.

clue.text: Intermediate, my French quarters

parts.note: mes is French for my before a plural noun
N and E are two compass quarters, north and east

explanation.surface: A Frenchman describes his middling lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Mesne is a legal term for something coming between two others, as a mesne lord stood between tenant and overlord.
explanation.definitionFit: In old law a mesne lord held land from a superior and granted it to a tenant, standing in the middle.

clue.text: Fellow leaves London road curiously to get bacon

leaves means goes away from, so the fellow's letters are taken out of the place name

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man walks off down a London street in search of a bacon sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes DON out of LONDON ROAD, leaving LONROAD, which 'curiously' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A lardoon is a strip of fat bacon threaded through lean meat before cooking.

clue.text: Poor Great Britain without money due to currency purchases

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so the letters for money are removed from the country's name

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Britain is short of cash because of buying foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes T, I and N from GREAT BRITAIN, leaving GREABRITA, which 'Poor' rearranges. 'Poor' reads as part of a lament for a broke nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrage is buying in one market to sell at once in another, often in foreign exchange, to profit from price gaps.

clue.text: Clown sees jetty decay

parts.note: a pier is a jetty jutting into the sea
rot is decay

explanation.surface: A seaside clown notices the pier crumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime.

clue.text: Impute a writer

parts.note: a scribe is a writer, especially a copyist

explanation.surface: Someone credits a piece of writing to an author.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute and to ascribe both mean attributing something to a cause or person.

clue.text: In which Barker may be trained

definitions.text: In which Barker may be trained

parts.words: In which Barker may be trained
parts.note: Barker reads as a surname, but a barker is a dog, which can be put through classes in doing as it is told

explanation.definitionFit: Dog training classes teach a pet to sit and stay on command, which is the virtue of doing as told.

clue.text: Winsome individual goes to island retreat

parts.note: an individual is a person

indicators.note: retreat means go back, so the island's name is read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: An attractive person heads off to an island hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns ELBA into ABLE. 'Island retreat' reads as a holiday hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome and personable both describe someone pleasant in manner and appearance.

clue.text: To some extent, coat hangers can be a curse

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wire coat hangers can be a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in cOAT Hangers.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a swear word as well as a solemn promise, so it can be a curse.

clue.text: Sailors from Epsom?

definitions.meaning: Epsom ... are the mineral crystals first taken from a spring at Epsom in Surrey

explanation.definitionFit: Veteran seamen are known as old salts, and the bath crystals named after Epsom in Surrey are Epsom salts.

clue.text: Addison's onlooker

definitions.meaning: Joseph Addison co-founded the London periodical The ... in 1711

clue.text: Of Jenny's case (The Merry Wives of Windsor)

parts.words: Of Jenny's case (The Merry Wives of Windsor)

clue.text: The cause of many a rising

definitions.text: The cause of many a rising

parts.words: The cause of many a rising

explanation.definitionFit: The military bugle call at dawn wakes soldiers and gets them up.

clue.text: Graceful as Lear's fowl

clue.text: Is one adjusted to sound?

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound, especially a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: Meantime, an edict of the German emperor

clue.text: Last year somewhat painful

explanation.surface: Last year was rather a painful one.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in laST YEar. The definition is an adjective while the answer is a noun: a stye is painful, the clue reading 'something painful'.

clue.text: A novice drops out of Oriental race possibly for amusement

indicators.note: possibly says the remaining letters are just one arrangement
drops out of says the named letters leave the phrase that follows

explanation.walkthrough: 'drops out of' removes A and L from ORIENTAL RACE, leaving ORIENTRACE, which 'possibly' rearranges.

clue.text: Always up entertaining English judge

indicators.note: entertaining means taking in as a guest, so one piece holds the other

explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EVER into REVE, and 'entertaining' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local magistrate or bailiff in medieval England, presiding over minor cases.

clue.text: Basket for wild single rose

clue.text: New master accepts the last vessel

clue.text: Together in action — it's a way of selling

definitions.text: Together in action — it's a way of selling

parts.words: Together in action — it's a way of selling

clue.text: Happy looking worker in the cloth industry?
